parsed.strategic_reason: The grant funds training and technical assistance to ensure the Title X and teen pregnancy prevention workforce can deliver high-quality family planning and reproductive health services, directly supporting NCDHHS's maternal and child health objective.
parsed.strategic_evidence_quote: The goal of the funded training center is to ensure that personnel working in Title X have the knowledge, skills, and self-efficacy necessary to effectively run a Title X grant program and deliver high-quality family planning services.
parsed.eligibility_evidence_quote: To receive funding from the Title X program, you must be a public or private non-profit entity.
parsed.operational_reason: DPH already administers family planning, maternal and child health, and provider training, but running a national training center for all OPA Title X and TPP grantees would be a major expansion beyond state-level responsibilities.
restrictions: Requires a single application covering both the Title X and TPP components, submitted under PA-FPT-25-001.
Cooperative agreement with two awards; multi-year projects require non-competing continuation applications for each budget period after the first.
Joint applications without a legally recognized relationship must contact OASH_Grants@hhs.gov and demonstrate conflict resolution capacity over the entire expected period of performance.
parsed.major_risk: The award is a single national training center for all OPA-funded Title X and TPP grantees, so NCDHHS would face strong national competition and must demonstrate capacity beyond North Carolina service delivery.
parsed.one_line_rationale: Strong topical fit with DPH family planning, but national training-center scope and single-award competition make it a low-yield pursuit for a state health agency.
